blocks.raw:
<Tip>**Quick Rule — Beam Determinacy:**
- **Simply Supported = Determinate** (2 unknowns, 3 equations, geometry stable)
- **Cantilever = Determinate** (3 unknowns, 3 equations; perfect match)
- **Continuous or Fixed-Ended = Indeterminate** (more than 3 unknowns)
- **Degree n = r − 3** (for unknowns r at supports; ignore joint unknowns if properly accounted)</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing determinacy with stability: A structure can be stable but indeterminate (continuous beam). It can also be determinate but unstable (three collinear supports). Determinacy and stability are separate properties.","Forgetting to count all unknowns: A fixed support has 3 unknowns (Hx, Hy, M), not just 1. A hinge has 2 unknowns. Miscounting leads to wrong determinacy assessment.","Assuming indeterminate structures are better: Indeterminate structures have redundancy, which is good. But they are also sensitive to support movement and thermal effects. Determinate structures are simpler to analyze but have no redundancy.","Ignoring the constraint that n = 0 is stable only if geometry is proper: Three hinges that are collinear form an unstable structure (n = 0 mathematically, but mechanism forms). Geometry and support arrangement matter.","Using the wrong equilibrium equations: In 3D, there are 6 equations of equilibrium. In 2D, there are 3. Applying 3D equations to a 2D problem leads to false indeterminacy counts."]} />
